records.summary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): Valparaíso/Viña: Chile's bohemian port-university culture; criminality is general rather than gender-targeted. Regional evidence: by a wide margin the country's highest-incidence region for anti-LGBTI discrimination - in 2024 it concentrated 51.32% of all national recorded cases (Metropolitana second at 25.12%), up 80.93% over 2023. In 2025 recorded cases fell here alongside Metropolitana while all 14 other regions rose; Movilh reads this as a decentralisation of hate toward territories with less LGBTIQ visibility and debate, not a local improvement. Scored relative to the national score (0.72) for Chile.

records.name: Bogota Capital District
records.summary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): Bogotá Capital District: the best-documented trans community and services in the country, alongside a documented police-violence pattern in its tolerance zone. Regional evidence: Red Comunitaria Trans reported police shouting at, baton-beating and shooting at trans sex workers at 3:50 a.m. on a central street (the district mayor's office took up the case); two trans women were killed within hours of each other on the night of 2 January 2026 (a 24-year-old in Engativá, a 20-year-old in Florida Blanca); a 32-year-old trans activist was found dead in the eastern hills in December 2023, with the press itself framing 'the recurring mechanisms in crimes against trans women'. The district's own law journal published a study of violence against trans people in the Santa Fe tolerance zone, where sector expulsions push people into other localities. Mass identity-check operations: 200+ officers in San Bernardo (April 2025) and over 1,200 uniformed officers with background and migrant control in Santa Fe (January 2026) - a visibly gender-nonconforming person in central Bogotá is therefore statistically likely to be in the path of a sweep. Scored relative to the national score (0.52) for Colombia.

records.name: Comunidad de Madrid
records.summary: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): Madrid (Chueca): among the most visible LGBT urban scenes in Europe; total anonymity in daily life; Pride among the continent's largest. Regional evidence: the one community that has used its own legislative power to narrow trans law - Ley 17/2023 and Ley 18/2023 (both 27 December 2023) amended the community's own 2016 gender-identity law and its anti-LGBTBI law on the stated ground of protecting freedom of expression and academic freedom, stripping the provisions that obliged educational institutions; Ley 1/2022 centres parents as primary responsible parties and structures school opt-outs (the 'pin parental' mechanism in Madrid schools). Evidentiary caveat: Madrid's citizens report LGTBI hate-crime offences to reporting services more than any other community's, so low recorded hostility here is not available as an alibi - the divergence is statutory, not statistical. Scored relative to the national score (0.88) for Spain.
